title: Zero-Trust Access Lifecycle and Procurement Alignment — Playbook and Templates
author: Aisha Morgan
body:
Overview:

This playbook defines the Zero-Trust Access Lifecycle used at Redwood Inference and prescribes how access decisions, change management, data handling, procurement approvals, and vendor onboarding must align. The goal is to reduce blast radius, maintain auditable approvals, and ensure procurement decisions reflect operational security and least-privilege requirements.

Intended audience:
- Engineering managers and platform owners
- Security reviewers and compliance owners
- Finance and procurement teams
- People Ops for role updates and offboarding

Scope:
- All systems and services that store or process customer or internal data (hosted, dedicated, private)
- User access patterns (person, service account, CI/CD token)
- Hardware and software procurement that will be onboarded to production or private deployments

High-level Principles:
1) Least-Privilege by Default: every grant should be scoped to the minimum resource and time necessary.
2) Explicit Approval and Traceability: all requests require approver identity, business justification, and expiration.
3) Separation of Duties: procurement approvals and technical provisioning require independent reviewers.
4) Continuous Verification: periodic entitlement review, automated attestations where possible.
5) Procurement Security Gate: any vendor or purchase that touches customer data or infra must pass a security checklist before ordering.

Definitions (short):
- Entitlement: permission granted to a principal to access a resource.
- Owner: the team responsible for the resource and first point of contact for approvals.
- Sensitive Resource: any asset categorized as PII, IP, or production-infrastructure.

Roles & Responsibilities:
- Requester: initiates access or procurement request with justification and expected duration.
- Resource Owner: validates technical need, selects grant scope, defines SRE/DR contact.
- Security Reviewer: evaluates the request for exposure, vendor risk, and compliance.
- Procurement/Finance Approver: verifies budget, contract terms, and vendor eligibility.
- People Ops: ensures role changes and terminations trigger entitlement revocation.

Access Lifecycle (Detailed Procedure):
1) Request Phase (Tooling: Access Portal / ServiceNow integration)
   - Requester populates: resource identifier (ARN or service name), purpose, least-privilege role, requested duration, and business justification.
   - Request must reference the ticket ID for any procurement tied to the access (e.g., new VM or external vendor account).

2) Approval Phase (two-step minimum for sensitive resources)
   - Step 1: Resource Owner approves scope & duration. For role-specific grants, the owner must select a pre-approved role template.
   - Step 2: Security Reviewer validates risk and selects compensating controls (MFA requirement, IP allowlist, monitoring hooks).
   - Step 3: Finance/Procurement approves if the access requires a new subscription, vendor account, or billed service.

3) Provisioning Phase (automation encouraged)
   - Automated provisioning preferred: IAM policy generated from templates, short-lived credentials, and audit log enablement.
   - Manual provisioning requires the provisioning engineer to attach the request ticket and record the change ID.

4) Active Use & Monitoring
   - All granted entitlements produce an audit event captured in the central logging pipeline.
   - Teams must create alerting for anomalous privilege elevation and high-volume data exports tied to newly-issued entitlements.

5) Expiration & Review
   - Every temporary grant is auto-expired at its requested end date.
   - Permanent grants must have an explicit quarterly attestation by the resource owner.
   - Annual entitlement review: owners receive the entitlement roster and must attest by the SLA date. Non-attested entitlements will be flagged for revocation.

6) Revocation & Offboarding
   - People Ops triggers revocation for terminated employees within 2 hours for production and 24 hours for non-prod.
   - For vendor contracts ending, the vendor account must be revoked and any keys rotated within 5 business days.

Change Management Intersection:
- Any change to access patterns that affects production or sensitive resources must follow the change control matrix: change category (minor/major/emergency), required approvers, rollout window, and backout plan.
- Example: Adding a new role that provides read access to billing data is a "major" change — requires Resource Owner, Security, and Finance signoff plus a canary rollout to a single user for 48 hours.
- Emergency changes (security patching, immediate revocation) must be recorded retroactively with documented justification and post-change review within 48 hours.

Procurement Alignment Checklist (applies pre-order):
- Does this purchase create new identities or vendor-managed accounts that will access Redwood infrastructure? If yes, attach vendor security checklist.
- Does the vendor process customer data? If yes, require contract clause with data processing addendum (DPA) and encryption requirements.
- Follow cost thresholds for approvals:
   - Under $5k: Team lead approval (documented in ticket).
   - $5k–$50k: Finance + Procurement approval.
   - >$50k: Finance + Procurement + VP-level approval and legal review.
- If hardware (GPU/servers) is procured for Dedicated or Private, include a network segmentation plan and KMS/HSM integration notes.

Vendor Security Gate (required artifacts before onboarding):
- Completed vendor security questionnaire and attestation to standards (ISO/ SOC / relevant checklist).
- Evidence of data handling controls: encryption in transit and at rest, access controls, logging retention.
- Contact matrix for incident response and escalation windows.
- Proof of required certifications or SOC2 reports if handling customer data.

Templates and Example Artifacts (copy/paste friendly fields):
1) Access Request Template (fields to capture in portal):
   - requester_name
   - team
   - resource_id (service/ARN)
   - access_role_template (link to role library)
   - justification (business)
   - desired_duration (ISO 8601)
   - linked_procurement_ticket (optional)
   - risk_mitigation (monitoring/MFA)

2) Procurement Fit-Gap Table (to be attached to vendor requests):
   - column headers: requirement | vendor_compliance | notes | evidence_link
   - sample rows: encryption-at-rest | yes/no | algorithm & key ownership | link-to-report

3) Approval Matrix (example):
   - team-lead: approve purchases <$5k and non-sensitive grants
   - procurement: approve purchases $5k–$50k and confirm vendor onboarding steps
   - finance-director: approve >$20k ongoing subscriptions
   - security: mandatory approver for any resource marked Sensitive or vendor-managed account
   - legal: mandatory for all customer-data-handling vendors and contracts >$50k

Operational Runbook Snippets (for oncall SREs):
- Revoke compromised key:
  1) Identify key ID and associated principals.
  2) Create revocation ticket in "Access Portal" referencing incident ID.
  3) Rotate any dependent keys, notify asset owner and security.
  4) Document actions and mark the incident for postmortem if exposure to customer data occurred.

- Emergency vendor account disablement:
  1) Security issues escalated to vendor-contact; disable account via vendor console or block IP ranges.
  2) Provision temporary alternative if service is essential; route traffic to fallback vendor if configured.
  3) Engage Legal and Procurement within 4 hours for contract remediation.

Data Management and Retention (short):
- Access decisions must reference the data classification for the resource. Data classification labels: Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted.
- Retention policies are applied at the dataset level; procurement of storage services requires agreeing to retention, deletion, and e-discovery terms.

Monitoring, Metrics & SLOs:
- Entitlement Review SLA: resource owners must attest to entitlements within 30 days of the attestation request (SLO 90%).
- Offboarding Revocation SLA: 2 hours for production accounts (SLO 99%), 24 hours for non-prod (SLO 95%).
- Vendor Onboarding Checklist Completion: 10 business days target from purchase approval to live onboarding (SLO 80%).

Audit and Evidence Collection:
- Every approval path must produce an immutable ticket with approver identity, timestamps, and justification.
- Security keeps 3 years of entitlement change logs for audit and internal review.

Example CLI snippets and IAM policy examples (illustrative):
- Short-lived token creation (example):
  $ accessctl issue --principal user:marcus --role read-only:billing --expires 72h --ticket TKT-12345

- Sample minimal IAM policy (text):
  {
    "Version": "2022-01-01",
    "Statement": [
      {
        "Effect": "Allow",
        "Action": ["billing:GetInvoices"],
        "Resource": ["arn:redwood:billing:prod:::invoices/*"]
      }
    ]
  }

Rollout and Adoption Plan:
1) Q2 2024: Pilot with Platform and Finance teams for procurement gating and short-lived access.
2) Q3 2024: Enforce automated expirations and connector integrations with People Ops.
3) Q4 2024: Expand enforcement to Dedicated and Private deployment onboarding flows.
4) Ongoing: Quarterly training for managers and procurement; update templates based on audit feedback.

Escalation Paths & Contacts:

Appendix: Example attestation email (one-click):
Subject: Quarterly Entitlement Attestation — Resource: billing-service
Body: Please confirm the list of active users and approve or mark for revocation. Link: <attestation-link>

Document maintenance:
- Owner (Security) will review annually or after any audit finding.
- Proposed changes appear as PRs in the policy repo; major updates require cross-functional signoff from Security, Finance, and People Ops.

End of document.
